key_concepts.name: Ready and set position
key_concepts.summary: The goalkeeper's ready position is an active stance that prepares immediate movement. The set position should appear before a shot or decisive action: feet grounded, weight forward, knees flexed, upper body strong, hands prepared, and eyes fixed on ball and cues.
coaching_cues: Move early, set before the strike.
Keep heels light and feet under the body.
Hands ready without locking the shoulders.
Reset after every adjustment step.

common_errors.error: Still moving as the shot is struck.
common_errors.correction: Coach a move-set-save rhythm and constrain shooters to punish late setting.

common_errors.error: Weight on heels or stance too narrow.
common_errors.correction: Use short lateral pushes from a shoulder-width stance and check whether both feet can push.

progression.beginner: Learn low athletic stance, balanced feet, hands ready, and simple saves from central service.
progression.intermediate: Set from shuffles, drops, recoveries, and angle changes before varied shots.
progression.advanced: Arrive set under realistic timing, screens, cutbacks, rebounds, and quick changes in shot location.

key_concepts.name: Handling and ball security
key_concepts.summary: Handling is not just catching. It includes body shape behind the ball, hand shape, soft absorption, secure collection before standing, deciding catch versus parry, and protecting the ball after contact.
coaching_cues: Eyes, hands, body behind the ball.
Secure first, then distribute.
Catch clean when possible; parry away from danger when catching is unrealistic.
Recover the ball before rising if the save is low.

common_errors.error: Trying to catch shots that must be deflected.
common_errors.correction: Teach catch, cushion, smother, parry-wide, and parry-over options by ball speed and traffic.

common_errors.error: Standing before the ball is secure.
common_errors.correction: Use low-ball drills where the rep is scored only after secure control and controlled rise.

progression.beginner: Chest-height catches, basket catches, low scoops, and simple collapse saves.
progression.intermediate: Add side movement, rebounds, varied ball speed, and distribution after secure handling.
progression.advanced: Handle through screens, wet/fast balls, deflections, contact pressure, and immediate counterattack decisions.

key_concepts.name: Shot stopping is positioning plus technique
key_concepts.summary: Shot stopping starts before the save. The goalkeeper adjusts their starting point, line to the ball, depth, angle, and set timing so the chosen technique has a realistic chance to succeed.
coaching_cues: Protect the goal first.
Travel on the ball movement, set on the shot cue.
Close the angle without opening a lob or cutback lane.
Use the body part that solves the shot fastest and safest.

common_errors.error: Treating every save as a dive.
common_errors.correction: Reward positioning saves, blocks, foot saves, smothers, and controlled catches.

common_errors.error: Drifting too far off the line against long-range shots.
common_errors.correction: Use shot-distance tasks that link depth to shooter angle, ball pressure, and lob risk.

progression.beginner: Central shot handling and basic angle play.
progression.intermediate: Near-post protection, cutbacks, low shots, and reaction saves from changing angles.
progression.advanced: Screened shots, rebounds, first-time finishes, close-range foot saves, and high-pressure penalty-area decisions.

key_concepts.name: Diving and safe landing
key_concepts.summary: Diving extends the goalkeeper's reach but adds impact load. Effective diving uses a ball-side push, appropriate step, lead hands, eyes through contact, body alignment, controlled landing, and quick recovery.
coaching_cues: Push through the ball-side leg.
Lead with hands, not the head.
Land along the side of the body, not flat on the shoulder or elbow.
Recover to feet or protect the ball based on the next threat.

common_errors.error: Belly-flop or elbow-first landing.
common_errors.correction: Regress to kneeling and low collapse progressions before full-extension dives.

common_errors.error: Diving when footwork would reach the ball.
common_errors.correction: Use small-goal or touchline constraints that reward step-and-catch before dive.

progression.beginner: Low collapse and scoop saves from kneeling or low ready positions.
progression.intermediate: Step-dive, low extension, mid-height extension, and recovery saves.
progression.advanced: Full-extension saves, deflections around posts, rebound recovery, and contact/traffic scenarios with strict load dosing.

key_concepts.name: Footwork connects perception to saves
key_concepts.summary: Goalkeeper footwork is the link between reading play and being set. Shuffles, small adjustment steps, drop steps, crossovers, recovery steps, and explosive first steps should move the goalkeeper without delaying the final set.
coaching_cues: Small steps near the shot, bigger steps to travel.
Do not cross feet when a shot can happen immediately.
Move with the ball, not after the shot.
Finish every movement balanced and set.

common_errors.error: Overstriding across goal and arriving off balance.
common_errors.correction: Use cone-to-shot tasks where the goalkeeper must freeze in set position before service.

common_errors.error: Static feet while the ball moves wide.
common_errors.correction: Train live ball movement and require continuous angle adjustment before the shot.

progression.beginner: Lateral shuffles and simple angle adjustments.
progression.intermediate: Cutback footwork, post-to-middle recovery, and explosive side pushes.
progression.advanced: Footwork through screens, second balls, set-piece traffic, and high-line sweeping decisions.

key_concepts.name: Crosses and aerial control
key_concepts.summary: Cross management combines starting position, scanning traffic, reading flight, timing, jump mechanics, communication, and intervention choice. Claiming gives possession, punching reduces immediate danger, tipping protects the goal when control is not possible, and staying can be correct when the cross is unreachable.
coaching_cues: Scan bodies before the delivery.
Read flight early, decide early, communicate clearly.
Claim only when you can secure the ball.
Punch with purpose away from central danger.

common_errors.error: Late indecision between claiming and staying.
common_errors.correction: Use cross zones and pressure levels that force a clear call before the ball drops.

common_errors.error: Jumping from a flat stance.
common_errors.correction: Set one foot slightly ahead when preparing for aerial take-off and attack the ball at the highest safe point.

progression.beginner: Unopposed high catch, basic call, and landing control.
progression.intermediate: Crosses from wide angles with passive then active traffic and distribution after catch.
progression.advanced: Corners, inswingers, outswingers, blockers, score-state decisions, and claim-punch-stay choices under contact pressure.

key_concepts.name: 1v1 situations
key_concepts.summary: In 1v1s the goalkeeper reduces the scoring picture while coordinating with recovering defenders. Decisions include hold, advance, block, spread, smother, delay, or stay, depending on ball distance, attacker touch, angle, defender pressure, and rebound risk.
coaching_cues: Read the attacker touch.
Close when the ball is loose or the angle is open.
Stay big and balanced for the finish cue.
Coordinate with the recovering defender rather than duplicating their action.

common_errors.error: Rushing at full speed when the attacker has close control.
common_errors.correction: Coach fast approach, braking, set/block shape, and delayed engagement.

common_errors.error: Going head-first into feet.
common_errors.correction: Teach safe smother technique only when the ball is clearly available and protect the head.

progression.beginner: Angle reduction and basic block shape from predictable service.
progression.intermediate: Live 1v1s with recovering defender, rebound, and pass-square options.
progression.advanced: High-speed through-ball races, disguised finishes, cutback threats, and transition to distribution after the save.

key_concepts.name: Distribution and build-up
key_concepts.summary: Modern goalkeeper distribution is an attacking and pressure-management skill. The goalkeeper offers at the right angle, scans before receiving, controls the first touch, and chooses the safest useful pass, throw, roll, clip, drive, or long release.
coaching_cues: Offer when the angle helps the team.
Scan before the ball arrives.
Play to the receiving player's advantage.
Break a line when the risk is justified; keep possession when it is not.

common_errors.error: Offering constantly without creating a useful angle.
common_errors.correction: Coach timed offers linked to defender body shape, pressure direction, and passing lane.

common_errors.error: Clearing long under pressure without assessing options.
common_errors.correction: Use pressed build-up games where short, medium, and long solutions are all available and scored by outcome.

progression.beginner: Rolling, underarm throws, simple passes, and safe restarts.
progression.intermediate: Back-pass receiving, first touch away from pressure, throws to advantage, and short goal-kick build-up.
progression.advanced: Line-breaking passes, disguise, third-player build-up, clipped passes over pressure, and tempo control.

key_concepts.name: Sweeper-keeper actions
key_concepts.summary: Sweeper-keeper play is the goalkeeper acting as depth cover behind the defensive line and as a support player in possession. It depends on line height, pressure on the ball, space behind defenders, starting distance from goal, acceleration, and shared defender understanding.
coaching_cues: Stay connected to the defensive line.
Read pressure on the passer before stepping high.
Advance decisively when the ball is playable and the attacker is through.
Do not create an empty-goal risk without pressure or cover.

common_errors.error: Standing deep while the team holds a high line.
common_errors.correction: Train goalkeeper line height with the back line in phase-of-play games.

common_errors.error: Sweeping when the defender can control the situation.
common_errors.correction: Use defend-goal, defend-space, support-defender decision cues.

progression.beginner: Understand penalty-area limits and when to stay close to goal.
progression.intermediate: Defend through balls inside the penalty area and support defenders as a passing option.
progression.advanced: Hold high starting positions, clear outside the penalty area with feet/head when lawful and safe, and coordinate with a high defensive line.

key_concepts.name: Communication and defensive organization
key_concepts.summary: Because the goalkeeper can see the full field more often than outfield players, they are central to organizing the defensive line, marking, set-piece responsibilities, pressure-cover cues, and emergency decisions.
coaching_cues: Use short, consistent commands.
Name the player and action when possible.
Communicate early enough for defenders to act.
Agree set-piece and line-management vocabulary in training.

common_errors.error: Long explanations during live danger.
common_errors.correction: Build a command dictionary for step, drop, hold, away, keeper, time, man, and turn.

common_errors.error: Only communicating after errors.
common_errors.correction: Score proactive information: line height, marking, pressure, and second-ball alerts.

progression.beginner: Call keeper/away, organize simple walls, and alert nearest defender.
progression.intermediate: Manage back-line depth, mark runners, call pressure/cover, and organize corners.
progression.advanced: Lead defensive organization through opponent-specific set plays, rest-defense cues, pressing triggers, and game-state tempo.

key_concepts.name: Goalkeeper law constraints
key_concepts.summary: Goalkeepers need technical solutions that respect the Laws. They can handle the ball inside their own penalty area except after certain deliberate team-mate actions, cannot handle outside the area, and under current IFAB law are penalized if they control the ball with the hands/arms for longer than eight seconds.
coaching_cues: Know when hands are unavailable.
Use feet confidently for back-passes.
Release quickly enough to avoid the eight-second limit.
Treat outside-area sweeping as an outfield action.

common_errors.error: Using hands on a deliberate back-pass or team-mate throw-in.
common_errors.correction: Train back-pass receiving with feet under pressure in every goalkeeper technical block.

common_errors.error: Holding the ball to manage tempo without awareness of the count.
common_errors.correction: Use possession-release games where the goalkeeper must scan, choose, and distribute within a timed window.

progression.beginner: Learn penalty-area handling limits and simple restarts.
progression.intermediate: Use feet for back-passes and choose safe goal-kick options.
progression.advanced: Use lawful tempo control, disguised restart speed, and pressure-resistant back-pass play.

key_concepts.name: Goalkeeper-specific physical profile
key_concepts.summary: Goalkeepers cover less high-intensity distance than many outfield roles but require sudden explosive actions: short accelerations, lateral pushes, dives, jumps, landings, throws, foot saves, and rapid recovery to set again.
coaching_cues: Train explosive quality without copying outfield conditioning volume.
Build landing and upper-limb tolerance before high dive volume.
Expose goalkeepers to match-like spikes late in sessions.
Monitor dives, jumps, explosive efforts, and shoulder/hand load.

common_errors.error: Preparing goalkeepers only with outfield running conditioning.
common_errors.correction: Add role-specific acceleration, lateral power, reaction, jump, dive, get-up, throwing, and mobility work.

common_errors.error: High repetition diving without load control.
common_errors.correction: Track dive contacts and vary technical, tactical, and low-impact days across the microcycle.

progression.beginner: Movement literacy, balance, coordination, safe falling, basic strength.
progression.intermediate: Explosive lateral power, landing control, upper-body resilience, repeated get-ups.
progression.advanced: High-force reactive saves, high-line accelerations, repeated explosive actions under fatigue, and individualized load management.

key_concepts.name: Goalkeeper as an integrated team player
key_concepts.summary: High-quality goalkeeper development is both specialist and integrated. Individual technique matters, but decision-making, build-up, defending space, set-piece organization, and communication only transfer when goalkeepers train with the team and defenders.
coaching_cues: Give the goalkeeper real team problems.
Blend specialist technical blocks with phase-of-play work.
Connect goalkeeper cues to the team's game model.
Include the goalkeeper in possession and defensive organization practices.

common_errors.error: Only training isolated shot-stopping.
common_errors.correction: Add game-context actions before and after the save: starting position, communication, rebound, distribution.

common_errors.error: Leaving the goalkeeper idle during team drills.
common_errors.correction: Design practices where the goalkeeper has a meaningful defensive, attacking, or organizing task.

progression.beginner: Rotate through outfield and goalkeeper experiences while learning fundamentals.
progression.intermediate: Combine goalkeeper-specific work with unit training and small-sided games.
progression.advanced: Align goalkeeper role to the team's press, build-up, rest defense, set pieces, and opposition plan.

tactical_rules.rule: If the attacker can shoot, the goalkeeper must prioritize being set before the strike over gaining one extra movement step.
tactical_rules.application: Use in shot stopping, cutbacks, volleys, rebounds, and box entries where the shot cue is imminent.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: If the ball is still traveling and the attacker cannot shoot yet, continue adjusting the angle before the final set.
source_refs: Goalkeeper explosiveness from the set position and goal prevention

tactical_rules.rule: The goalkeeper's starting position should stay connected to the defensive line and ball pressure.
tactical_rules.application: Higher defensive line and pressure on the ball allow a higher goalkeeper position; no pressure on the passer or an exposed goal requires a more conservative depth.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Do not stand high if a direct shot or uncontested pass over the goalkeeper is realistic.
source_refs: FIFA Insight episode 3: Goalkeeper distribution, positioning and offering
Goalkeeper's decision-making and positioning when defending the space

tactical_rules.rule: When the defensive line is threatened, choose one primary task: defend the goal, defend the space, or support the defender.
tactical_rules.application: The decision depends on the nearest defender's position, pressure on the ball carrier, the attacker's access to goal, and the goalkeeper's relation to goal line and defensive line.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Avoid mixed decisions such as half-advancing and stopping unless the ball state changes.
source_refs: Goalkeeper's decision-making and positioning when defending the space

tactical_rules.rule: In 1v1s, coordinate with the recovering defender so one player pressures the ball while the other protects the goal, cutback, or rebound lane.
tactical_rules.application: Relevant for breakaways, box entries, and saves where a defender can recover to the line or block a square pass.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Avoid both goalkeeper and defender attacking the same ball if it exposes a simple pass or rebound.

tactical_rules.rule: From crosses and corners, claim only when secure control is likely; punch when the ball can be cleared better than caught; stay when late arrival or traffic makes intervention riskier than defending the goal.
tactical_rules.application: Use with inswingers, outswingers, crowded six-yard boxes, blockers, and score-state situations.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Avoid a late, uncertain claim that creates collision or central spill risk.
source_refs: Goalkeeping: Dealing with crosses from corners

tactical_rules.rule: Every cross intervention needs a second-ball plan.
tactical_rules.application: If the goalkeeper punches, tips, spills, or is blocked from claiming, defenders must know who protects goal line, near post, far post, penalty spot, and edge of box.
source_refs: Goalkeeping: Dealing with crosses from corners

tactical_rules.rule: Distribution should either retain possession securely or break an opposition line with acceptable risk.
tactical_rules.application: Classify the action as around, through, into, onto, or beyond, then assess whether the pass/throw matched pressure, receiver body shape, and team support.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Avoid long clearances that surrender possession when a safe support option or line-breaking pass is available.

tactical_rules.rule: The goalkeeper should offer to receive only when the angle, body shape, and pressure picture create a real solution for the team.
tactical_rules.application: Use in goal kicks, back-pass support, pressed build-up, and when defenders need an escape pass.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Avoid offering behind a closed passing lane or receiving square under pressure with no next option.

tactical_rules.rule: After clean possession, the goalkeeper controls tempo: quick release against disorganized opponents, pause and organize when the team needs rest or shape, within law limits.
tactical_rules.application: Use after catches, smothers, back-pass control, and set-piece claims.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Do not exceed current law limits for hand control or delay goal kicks.

tactical_rules.rule: Goalkeepers must treat deliberate team-mate kicks and throw-ins as foot-play situations, not handling opportunities.
tactical_rules.application: Train receiving, first touch, disguise, passing, clearing, and pressure escape with both feet.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Avoid hands on deliberate back-passes or direct team-mate throw-ins inside the penalty area.

tactical_rules.rule: When the goalkeeper controls the ball with the hands or arms inside the penalty area, scan and distribute quickly enough to stay within the current eight-second IFAB limit.
tactical_rules.application: Use in possession-release training and game-state tempo coaching.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Avoid outdated six-second coaching language unless a local competition explicitly uses an older rule set.
source_refs: Law 12 - Fouls and Misconduct

tactical_rules.rule: Goalkeeper training should include specialist technique and integrated team situations that reflect the team's game model.
tactical_rules.application: Pair handling, diving, and crossing blocks with defenders, build-up patterns, set pieces, pressing schemes, and transition games.
tactical_rules.avoid_when: Avoid isolating the goalkeeper for an entire session when the target behavior depends on defenders and team cues.
source_refs: UEFA Goalkeeper Coaching: An integrated and collaborative approach

physical_demands.demand: Explosive lateral force production from a set stance.
physical_demands.details: Shot stopping and diving require rapid pushes from either leg while the goalkeeper remains balanced enough to adjust to ball movement.

physical_demands.demand: Short explosive acceleration for 1v1s, through balls, and space defense.
physical_demands.details: Sweeper-keeper actions are usually short sprints or sharp accelerations rather than long running volume.

physical_demands.demand: Repeated dive, landing, and get-up actions.
physical_demands.details: Goalkeeper-specific training can produce much higher dive counts than many other activities, so dive volume and landing quality need planned progression.

physical_demands.demand: Jumping, reaching, catching, punching, and landing under aerial pressure.
physical_demands.details: Crosses and corners require vertical or diagonal take-off, upper-body reach, contact tolerance, safe landing, and immediate second-ball organization.

physical_demands.demand: High shoulder, elbow, wrist, finger, and grip demand.
physical_demands.details: Catching, punching, throwing, diving contact, and ball impact place more upper-limb demand on goalkeepers than most outfield roles.
source_refs: Injuries and Pain Associated with Goalkeeping in Football - Review of the Literature

physical_demands.demand: Repeated low stance, braking, and reactive repositioning.
physical_demands.details: Ready positions, cutbacks, and close-range saves require the goalkeeper to hold and adjust low positions while staying reactive.

physical_demands.demand: Low average locomotor intensity with sudden high-intensity actions.
physical_demands.details: Match analysis shows goalkeepers often spend a large share of match movement at low intensity, but decisive moments require explosive actions, technical accuracy, and concentration after inactivity.

physical_demands.demand: Rapid perception, anticipation, decision-making, and communication.

physical_demands.demand: Blend of mobility, maximal strength, explosive power, coordination, balance, and flexibility.
physical_demands.details: The goalkeeper profile requires strength and power for explosive actions, mobility for low and wide positions, and coordination for safe landing and ball control.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Diving landings, punches, catches, throws, and sharp shots can overload or injure shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands, and fingers.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Progress catch speed, dive height, punch volume, and throwing load gradually; include shoulder control, wrist/finger preparation, and safe landing mechanics.
source_refs: Injuries and Pain Associated with Goalkeeping in Football - Review of the Literature

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Poor catching technique, oversized or overinflated balls for youth, hard shots, and awkward ground contact increase finger, thumb, and wrist injury risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Teach correct hand shape and cushioning, use age-appropriate balls, reduce high-speed service for beginners, and add progressive grip and wrist robustness.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Repeated side landings during diving can irritate the shoulder, arm, ribs, hip, and trunk, especially when technique or surface quality is poor.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Build low dive progressions, vary training surfaces when possible, dose full-extension work, and monitor pain from repeated impact.
source_refs: Injuries and Pain Associated with Goalkeeping in Football - Review of the Literature

injury_or_load_risks.risk: 1v1 smothers, aerial challenges, contact with opponents, ground impact, and goalpost proximity can create head and concussion risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Avoid head-first challenges unless the ball is clearly available, teach safe 1v1 body shape, enforce concussion protocols, and design goals and posts safely.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Wide spread saves, lateral pushes, high split-like positions, side dives, and repeated kicking can overload hip, groin, and adductor tissues.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Progress lateral range and strength, include adductor and hip capacity work, and avoid sudden spikes in spread-save and lateral dive volume.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Explosive lateral pushes, close-range blocks, quick braking, jumping, and landing can stress knee, ankle, Achilles, and calf structures.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Build lower-limb strength, ankle stiffness, landing mechanics, and deceleration capacity; avoid fatigue-heavy plyometric doses before matches.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Goalkeeper-only sessions may create high dive, jump, throw, and explosive-effort volume that is not visible in team GPS distance totals.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Track role-specific counts such as dives, jumps, high-load landings, throws, explosive efforts, and get-ups across the microcycle.
source_refs: The physical demands of professional soccer goalkeepers throughout a week-long competitive microcycle and transiently throughout match-play

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Small pitches and frequent restarts can overload goalkeepers through repeated shots, saves, accelerations, and distributions in short periods.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use SSG size intentionally: small areas for high involvement with controlled duration, larger areas for team shape and spatial decisions.
source_refs: Physical and Tactical Demands of the Goalkeeper in Football in Different Small-Sided Games

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Crowded corners and crosses expose goalkeepers to aerial collisions, blockers, landing on players, and being impeded while airborne.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Train communication, take-off timing, safe landing, claim-versus-punch decisions, and second-ball roles under progressive traffic.
source_refs: Goalkeeping: Dealing with crosses from corners

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Young goalkeepers may fear contact, dives, hard shots, and crosses; growth and maturation changes can temporarily affect coordination, reach, and landing tolerance.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use age-appropriate balls, lower impact progressions, positive repetition, rotation with outfield play, and staged exposure to contact and aerial pressure.
source_refs: National Goalkeeping Course
Goalkeeping session: the basics

training_implications.implication: Goalkeepers need team-context practice as well as specialist technical work.
training_implications.application: Build sessions where the goalkeeper handles shots, organizes defenders, supports build-up, defends space, and distributes after the action.
source_refs: UEFA Goalkeeper Coaching: An integrated and collaborative approach
In safe hands: incorporating the goalkeeper into your practices

training_implications.implication: The ready position must be trained dynamically.
training_implications.application: Serve from moving ball situations, require angle adjustment, and score whether the goalkeeper is set at the shot cue.
source_refs: Goalkeeper explosiveness from the set position and goal prevention

training_implications.implication: Beginner goalkeepers should learn safe handling and catching confidence before high-velocity shot volume.
training_implications.application: Use clean service, appropriate ball size, low-to-mid catches, and distribution after secure handling before adding pressure and speed.
source_refs: Goalkeeping session: the basics

training_implications.implication: Diving should begin as safe falling and landing skill, then become explosive reach.
training_implications.application: Start with low collapse saves, then step-dive, then extension, then live rebound and contact scenarios.
source_refs: Injuries and Pain Associated with Goalkeeping in Football - Review of the Literature

training_implications.implication: Cross training must include claim, punch, tip, stay, and second-ball decisions.
training_implications.application: Change delivery type, traffic, blockers, and score state so the goalkeeper learns when aggression is useful and when staying protects the goal.
source_refs: Goalkeeping: Dealing with crosses from corners

training_implications.implication: Distribution quality should be trained with pressure and next-action context.
training_implications.application: Use pressed build-up games where the goalkeeper offers to receive, scans, takes the first touch away from pressure, and chooses around, through, into, onto, or beyond.
source_refs: Goalkeepers take a more strategic approach to offering, receiving and distributing the ball
Goalkeeping distribution styles

training_implications.implication: Defending space and 1v1s depend on a shared goalkeeper-defender relationship.
training_implications.application: Train through-ball and 1v1 scenarios with recovering defenders, including explicit roles for line cover, cutback, and goalkeeper advance.
source_refs: Goalkeeper's decision-making and positioning when defending the space

training_implications.implication: Goalkeeper load cannot be judged by total distance alone.
training_implications.application: Track dives, high-load dives, jumps, explosive efforts, get-ups, throws, shoulder symptoms, hand impacts, and late-session quality.
source_refs: The physical demands of professional soccer goalkeepers throughout a week-long competitive microcycle and transiently throughout match-play

training_implications.implication: Small-sided games can either overload or underprepare a goalkeeper depending on pitch size and rules.
training_implications.application: Use small formats for frequent shots and distributions, larger formats for sweeping and team connection, and restart rules that match the training aim.
source_refs: Physical and Tactical Demands of the Goalkeeper in Football in Different Small-Sided Games

training_implications.implication: Back-pass, handling-area, and hand-control time laws should shape goalkeeper technique.
training_implications.application: Include back-pass receiving with both feet, outside-area clearances without hands, timed hand-control releases, and goal-kick build-up scenarios.
source_refs: Law 12 - Fouls and Misconduct
Goalkeepers

training_implications.implication: Goalkeeper assessment should include technical, tactical, physical, social, psychological, and perceptual-cognitive domains.
training_implications.application: Track set timing, handling security, cross decisions, distribution, sweeping, communication, bravery, concentration, coachability, and decision quality.
source_refs: 'Goalkeepers are players too': key attributes coaches look for in talented youth soccer goalkeepers

training_implications.implication: Goalkeeper S&C should develop explosive power and robustness without unnecessary outfield running volume.
training_implications.application: Prioritize lower-limb power, lateral movement, trunk stiffness, shoulder resilience, hip mobility, reactive agility, and recovery across the match week.
source_refs: The physical demands of professional soccer goalkeepers throughout a week-long competitive microcycle and transiently throughout match-play
